10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-05 / SPK-04 — the internal image and the sandbox, in-cluster AC-2b [ED-05, SPK-04, Platform/SRE] — the same pod spec APPLIED, with Chromium’s sandbox observed active in-cluster: non-root under the cluster PodSecurity level, unprivileged user namespaces on the nodes, launch logs showing the sandbox active with no disabling flag, /dev/shm sized sufficiently, and a controlled-fixture run producing a readable webm from that pod. CARRIES story 10.12 AC-6b. There is NO fallback that disables the sandbox: if neither RuntimeDefault nor a Platform-approved Localhost profile works, this escalates to Platform/SRE and Security. Closes when docs/qa/spikes/SPK-04/ carries the evidence and ED-05 is updated.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-05 / SPK-04 — the internal image and the sandbox, in-cluster AC-3b [SPK-04 question 3, Platform/SRE + @architect] — the seccomp profile the spike selects, with its approval reference: whether RuntimeDefault permits the namespace-creating clone/unshare calls the sandbox needs without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and if not, the Platform-approved Localhost profile file, its owner and its approval reference, committed under docs/qa/spikes/SPK-04/. ADR-001 open item O-4. The chart renders RuntimeDefault as a deliberate starting value, never inherited from the backend and never Unconfined.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-05 / SPK-04 — the internal image and the sandbox, in-cluster AC-4b [ED-05, SPK-04, Platform/SRE] — SEC-2 browser-path immutability on the INTERNAL image in-cluster, rather than on the public Playwright base ADR-001 §8 permits for local development only. The attack itself is run and recorded against the local image in test/deployment/sec2.test.ts; what is deferred is running it against the image ED-05 delivers, inside a pod. CARRIES story 10.12 AC-6b with AC-2b.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-05 / SPK-04 — the internal image and the sandbox, in-cluster AC-5b [SPK-04 question 6, Platform/SRE] — in-cluster PID-1 reaping and slot recovery: under shareProcessNamespace, an orphaned grandchild is reaped by the pause container and a hung child is killed by the parent with the pod recovering its slot. CARRIES story 10.13 AC-11b. The mechanism is chosen and rendered (shareProcessNamespace: true) and the SIGNAL half is proven against the built image in 10.18a; the REAPING half cannot be proven outside a pod, because a pause container exists only in one. Stated rather than blurred, as AC-5a requires.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-04 / SPK-05 — egress enforcement and destination policy AC-8b [ED-04, SPK-05, Platform/SRE + an unnamed application owner] — enforcement proven FROM a runner pod with the policy applied: approved host reachable; unapproved host blocked; REDIRECT to an unapproved host blocked; subresources and authentication-provider hops to approved hosts allowed; cloud/cluster metadata and control endpoints, link-local ranges and local files unreachable; DNS behaviour for an unapproved name recorded; callback and object store reachable. If the spike finds only static L3/L4 policy exists, §9.3 requires that per-run destination checks in the runner become the PRIMARY control and that Security accept that limitation EXPLICITLY — that acceptance, or its absence, is part of this criterion’s evidence.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-04 / SPK-05 — egress enforcement and destination policy AC-9b [ED-04, ADR-002 O-6, @architect then the implementing story] — story 10.17’s destination-misuse negative tests, un-skipped against the enforced mechanism. They are 10.17’s tests, in 10.17’s files, and this story does not rewrite them. CARRIES story 10.17 AC-16b with its gate note unchanged. The gate-shut tripwire over the production ACCEPTED_JOB_KEYS is re-run UNCHANGED and green in test/run/canary.test.ts; adding a policy field to the closed RunJob is ADR-002 Class B and no story may land it before an architect rules.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-03 / SPK-03 — the private object store AC-10b [ED-03, SPK-03, Platform/SRE] — the scopes DENIED IN FACT on the real store: the runner principal’s GET and LIST denied, the API principal’s PUT denied; plus path-style addressing, multipart upload, HEAD/GET with Range, server-side encryption defaults, and read-after-write consistency on a key the recovery path reads immediately after writing. CARRIES story 10.14 AC-18b. The DEPLOYMENT half — two distinct Secrets, no Get/List key name on the runner’s side, the fixed §6.2 prefix — is asserted over the rendered manifest in test/deployment/chart.test.ts. What is deferred is a denial observed on a real store.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-03 / SPK-03 — the private object store AC-11 [ED-03, SPK-03, Platform/SRE] — lifecycle, versioning and incomplete-upload behaviour with caveats recorded: whether bucket versioning is on and whether lifecycle rules expire noncurrent versions and delete markers; whether incomplete multipart uploads are aborted and after how long; the observed lag between lifecycle expiry and physical deletion; and whether a GET on an expired object fails or still serves. CARRIES story 10.14 AC-19b. A NEGATIVE result is a valid closure and is recorded as a caveat for Security, not worked around. Until then no artefact may claim exact-time physical deletion — asserted over this story’s own rendered output in chart.test.ts.

10.18a — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-02 — identity, and the halves inherited from stories 10.7 and 10.17 AC-19b [ED-02, owner UNASSIGNED IN SOURCES] — credentialed acceptance through the real ingress: a real trusted-gateway identity resolving to a real user; a FORGED identity header denied at the gateway rather than at the application; a wrong-CSI request denied; access revocation terminating an open SSE stream within the configured refresh interval; and the real vault replacing the SecretsService REDACTED/plaintext stub. CARRIES story 10.17 AC-5b and AC-7b, and story 10.7 AC-4b, AC-6b and AC-37b. The CODE half (three bypass paths made configuration-driven and default-closed) is story 10.18b’s. @po could not name an owner and said so; @pm raises ED-02 to Checks-squad engineering management via BRD §8, with Security & Compliance accepting. Story 10.19 MAY NOT BE DRAFTED while ED-02’s owner reads TBD.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-13b [ED-06, SPK-02 question 3, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — TWO TIMED execution.snapshot EVENTS REACH A REAL BROWSER SEPARATELY, before response closure, through every proxy layer, captured as a HAR from a real browser on the staging hosts. The DEPLOYMENT half is done and asserted over the rendered manifest: a separate Ingress carrying only the two streaming paths, proxy-buffering off, and an idle timeout derived from the stream lifetime and compared against the rendered heartbeat in the same manifest. What is deferred is whether any of that survives the wire. A PASSING BACKEND TEST IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS CRITERION and must not be offered as one — the SSE assessment says so directly: "a buffered mock-controller response does not prove SSE delivery". Closes when docs/qa/spikes/SPK-02/ carries the HAR and ED-06 is updated.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-14 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 4, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — a 15 s HEARTBEAT KEEPS AN IDLE STREAM OPEN across the ingress and any platform proxy, and the EFFECTIVE MAXIMUM STREAM LIFETIME is measured against the intended 60 s. If the effective maximum is BELOW the configured lifetime, the configured value moves to match the measurement and the change is recorded — studioSse.lifetimeSeconds is a §8.5 starting value, not a commitment, and the ingress timeout is derived from it so it moves too. That is the mechanism working, not a criterion failing. Nothing in this repository can measure a proxy it has never crossed.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-15 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 5, Platform/SRE (ingress) + backend dev] — RECONNECT WITH Last-Event-ID TO A DIFFERENT API REPLICA restores the current snapshot. The evidence must show the two connections were served by DIFFERENT PODS: a reconnect that happens to land on the same replica proves nothing and is the way this criterion gets reported passed without being tested. Production runs three replicas scaling to six. The design answers this by reading committed state rather than by affinity, and **NO STICKY-SESSION OR SESSION-AFFINITY SETTING MAY BE INTRODUCED TO MAKE IT PASS** — story 10.18b introduced none, and the streaming Ingress it added carries no affinity annotation of any kind. Trading a design property for a deployment workaround would close this criterion by defeating the thing it exists to check.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-16b [ED-06, SPK-02 questions 1-2, Platform/SRE (ingress) + frontend dev] — THE PLATFORM’S ACTUAL BROWSER-AUTH ROUTE, IN WRITING, COVERING FEDERATED MODE: which route carries the session cookie to the events and video paths — same-origin gateway path, or cross-origin with withCredentials plus exact-origin credentialed CORS — and whether it holds in BOTH standalone and federated (shell-hosted) modes, where the browser’s origin is the PUT platform shell’s and no values file in this chart can know it; and whether a bearer-only requirement exists anywhere on the path, in which case SSE needs the header-capable client inside the centralized API service (STORY 10.11’s, not this one’s) and <video> needs an ambient session regardless. The DEPLOYMENT half is done: exact-origin credentialed CORS compared against the rendered frontend host in the same manifest, never a wildcard, and no credential in any URL. A DEMONSTRATED GATEWAY INCOMPATIBILITY IS A VALID OUTCOME — it selects the documented GET fallback and changes no execution contract.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-21b [ED-06 / SPK-02 question 7, and ED-02; Platform/SRE + Security] — THE CSRF CONTROL THE PLATFORM ROUTE ACTUALLY PROVIDES, stated in writing by its owner, and whether the application must add one. The DECIDABLE half is done (AC-21a): the gap is recorded with the two facts that bound it — the put_session cookie and SecurityConfig.setAllowCredentials(true) with the MFE and API on different hosts — in SecurityConfig itself and in the runbook §10 as an open launch prerequisite. This story deliberately did NOT enable Spring’s CSRF filter or drop CORS credentials: either changes the public request contract of every existing Checks route, which is not a Studio story’s to land.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed Staging — the deployed stack under load AC-23b [staging; ED-06/ED-05 and the spikes; Platform/SRE] — KILL SWITCH, DRAIN, RECOVERY AND BOUNDED OVERLOAD OBSERVED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED STACK, with ordinary REST/check service preserved. Bounded Studio load must not degrade the ordinary check path — a BRD success metric, not a nicety — and pod sizing is validated under that load before production templating (BRD §8: "Prove one runner pod in staging before templating production"). The kill switch’s behaviour is driven on the production path in both directions in backend StudioKillSwitchWiringTest, and its deployed wiring is asserted over the rendered manifest; what is deferred is the stack.
